title: Multilingual RAG Knowledge Assistant for Documents & Learning Content
one_liner: Turn multilingual PDFs, presentations, and visual documents into a searchable, citation-backed AI knowledge assistant with image-aware retrieval and question generation.
problem: Teams and learners often work with large collections of PDFs, presentations, scanned pages, and visual documents. Finding the right information, tracing answers back to the source, and generating useful study or review material manually is slow and error-prone.
approach: Built a RAG-based knowledge system for PDFs and PowerPoint files containing multilingual text, diagrams, and slide images
Extracted and indexed content with page-level and slide-level references so generated answers could be traced back to the original source
Added image-aware referencing to connect responses with relevant diagrams, figures, and visual document content
Used ChromaDB for semantic vector retrieval across large document collections
Integrated Gemini models for context-aware question answering, reasoning, and multilingual response generation
Created an interactive dashboard with local knowledge-base search and optional internet-based source mode
Added configurable question and MCQ generation for learning, assessment, and review workflows
results: Created a reusable document knowledge assistant for large, mixed-format information collections
Enabled citation-backed answers with PDF page and PowerPoint slide references for improved trust and traceability
Supported multilingual search and generation across English, French, and German content
Added automated question generation for training, assessment, and knowledge-review use cases
Delivered an interactive workflow suitable for education, internal knowledge bases, and document-heavy business processes

title: Document AI for Intelligent Data Extraction
one_liner: Extract structured business data from PDFs, scans, and semi-structured documents using OCR, layout analysis, NLP, and API-ready validation.
problem: Organizations receive documents in inconsistent formats, layouts, and scan qualities. Manual extraction is expensive, while rigid template-based systems often fail when fields move or document structures change.
approach: Built a reusable extraction pipeline combining OCR, layout analysis, and field-detection logic
Applied rule-based, NLP, and machine-learning methods where each approach was most effective
Normalized and validated extracted values before producing structured JSON and CSV outputs
Prepared the workflow for integration with APIs, analytics systems, and downstream business automation
results: Created a flexible document-processing workflow that can adapt across multiple template variants
Reduced manual effort required to convert unstructured documents into structured application data
Produced integration-ready outputs suitable for automation, analytics, and internal software systems

title: AI-Powered SaaS Platform with Human-in-the-Loop Workflows
one_liner: Built and integrated AI-assisted workflows inside a full-stack SaaS product, contributing across LLM features, Lovable frontend development, database integration, APIs, and QA-driven delivery.
problem: Modern SaaS products increasingly need AI features that work reliably inside real user workflows rather than as isolated demos. The challenge was to combine user-facing interfaces, persistent application data, backend services, and reviewable AI outputs in one production-oriented system.
approach: Developed AI-assisted workflows that transformed application data into summaries, structured drafts, recommendations, and actionable insights
Worked on LLM prompting and structured output generation for application-ready AI responses
Implemented and refined user-facing interfaces using Lovable together with frontend code
Connected frontend functionality with persistent database-backed workflows
Integrated AI features with backend APIs and application data flows
Collaborated closely with backend developers on API contracts, data structures, debugging, and end-to-end feature behavior
Worked with QA to reproduce issues, validate AI and frontend behavior, test edge cases, and improve release quality
Applied human-in-the-loop patterns so generated outputs remained reviewable and editable before final use
results: Delivered AI capabilities as part of a complete multi-user SaaS application rather than standalone prototypes
Connected AI, frontend, database, and backend services into practical end-to-end user workflows
Improved product reliability through iterative testing and close collaboration with QA and backend engineering
Implemented reviewable AI interactions suited to business processes where human oversight is important
Demonstrated cross-functional product development across AI integration, UI implementation, databases, APIs, testing, and delivery

title: Video RAG for Searchable Long-Form Content
one_liner: Turn long videos into a searchable knowledge base by combining transcript processing, semantic retrieval, and retrieval-grounded question answering.
problem: Important information inside meetings, lectures, webinars, interviews, and recordings is difficult to retrieve when users must manually scrub through long videos.
approach: Extracted transcripts and divided long-form video content into semantically meaningful segments
Indexed segment-level text with embeddings for accurate semantic search
Mapped retrieved text back to relevant moments in the source content
Generated answers from the most relevant retrieved segments instead of processing the full recording for every query
results: Created a reusable searchable-video knowledge workflow for long-form recordings
Reduced the time required to find specific topics and answers inside video content
Established a practical RAG pattern for meetings, training videos, lectures, and media archives

title: Data-Grounded LLM Content Generation Platform
one_liner: Generate domain-specific content from connected knowledge sources through a controllable, review-friendly LLM application.
problem: Businesses need AI-generated content that reflects their own information, follows constraints, and remains easy to review before it is published, shared, or used in an operational workflow.
approach: Grounded generation with retrieval from custom knowledge sources and structured contextual data
Added prompt templates, tone controls, and output constraints to improve consistency
Connected the generation workflow with database-backed content and application logic
Built a user interface for drafting, reviewing, editing, and exporting generated content
results: Delivered more consistent and context-aware text generation for domain-specific workflows
Created a reusable pattern for internal writing assistants, reporting tools, and content-generation applications
Made LLM-based content generation accessible to non-technical users through a review-oriented interface

title: Custom Image Generation with LoRA + Stable Diffusion
one_liner: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion with LoRA to preserve custom visual identities, styles, or subjects across prompts, poses, and scenes.
problem: Generative-image applications often need a subject, product, character, or visual style to remain consistent across many outputs, but standard generation can drift in appearance between prompts.
approach: Prepared focused image datasets for parameter-efficient Stable Diffusion adaptation
Fine-tuned LoRA models to improve identity and style consistency across generations
Refined prompts and inference settings to control composition, appearance, and repeatability
results: Improved consistency of recurring visual subjects across different prompts and scenes
Built a reusable fine-tuning workflow for custom creative, branding, and content-generation use cases

title: Semantic Matching & Ranking with Transformer Embeddings
one_liner: Match and rank text records using transformer embeddings, semantic similarity, scoring logic, and explainable gap analysis.
problem: Many ranking and recommendation workflows rely too heavily on exact keyword overlap, even when two records express the same concepts using different language.
approach: Extracted domain-relevant entities, terms, and text signals with NLP pipelines
Computed semantic alignment using transformer embeddings and vector-similarity methods
Combined semantic similarity with scoring and ranking logic for more useful matches
Added explainable missing-signal or gap feedback to make ranking results more actionable
results: Produced more informative semantic matching than keyword overlap alone
Created a reusable ranking pipeline applicable to recruitment, search, recommendations, and record matching
Added explainable feedback that helps users understand why items rank highly or where important information is missing

title: Entity Extraction & Human Review Tool for Scanned Documents
one_liner: Extract structured entities from scanned documents and route uncertain outputs through a human-review interface before export.
problem: Important fields in real-world documents can be fragmented, noisy, inconsistently formatted, or partially obscured, which makes fully automated extraction unreliable.
approach: Located candidate information regions using OCR and layout-aware heuristics
Structured extracted components with NER, vision APIs, and rule-based parsing logic
Added confidence-aware validation and a correction interface for uncertain outputs
Prepared reviewed results for downstream APIs and business systems
results: Created a practical extraction workflow for noisy and inconsistent scanned documents
Added a human-in-the-loop review path for higher-confidence operational use
Built a reusable pattern for extracting addresses, identifiers, names, and other structured entities

title: End-to-End ML Prediction Dashboard with API Serving
one_liner: Train, compare, serve, and visualize machine-learning models through REST APIs and an interactive application dashboard.
problem: Machine-learning models are most useful when predictions can be served reliably, compared clearly, and reviewed through an interface accessible to non-technical stakeholders.
approach: Trained and compared multiple machine-learning and deep-learning model families for prediction tasks
Built REST API endpoints for online and batch inference workflows
Connected models with persistent data and application-level prediction pipelines
Created dashboard views for predictions, evaluation metrics, and model-facing interaction
results: Delivered an end-to-end workflow from model development to API-based prediction and visualization
Created a reusable architecture for production-style ML applications and proof-of-concept dashboards
Made model outputs easier for non-technical stakeholders to inspect and compare

title: Natural-Language Data Assistant with PostgreSQL + GPT
one_liner: Let users query structured database information in natural language and receive clear, application-ready responses through an LLM-powered data assistant.
problem: Business users often need insights from structured data but cannot efficiently write SQL or translate every question into database operations.
approach: Stored structured data in PostgreSQL and organized it for reliable querying
Combined retrieval, database access, and LLM reasoning to interpret natural-language questions
Converted user questions into context-aware data interactions
Returned formatted responses designed for dashboards, APIs, and decision-support interfaces
results: Created a natural-language access layer for structured PostgreSQL datasets
Built a reusable pattern for database-backed AI assistants across business domains
Reduced the technical barrier between end users and structured operational data

title: AI Workflow Automation with n8n, APIs & LLMs
one_liner: Automate repetitive business processes by connecting triggers, APIs, databases, webhooks, and LLM-based decision or processing steps in n8n.
problem: Teams often spend time manually moving information between applications, enriching data, sending notifications, and repeating predictable operational tasks.
approach: Built trigger-driven workflows that ingest, process, store, and route information across connected services
Integrated LLMs, REST APIs, webhooks, databases, and custom processing steps into reusable automations
Added branching logic, retries, logging, and failure-aware handling for more reliable execution
Structured workflows so individual components could be adapted to different business processes
results: Reduced repetitive manual work in AI-assisted business operations
Created reusable automation patterns for lead handling, document processing, notifications, content workflows, and data enrichment
Improved reliability through explicit error handling and observable workflow execution

title: Human Pose Tracking & Action Recognition from Video
one_liner: Track human pose across challenging video and classify actions using temporal motion features and deep-learning pipelines.
problem: Human activity recognition becomes difficult when videos contain fast movement, camera motion, occlusion, changing viewpoints, or noisy keypoint detections.
approach: Implemented and compared multiple pose-estimation backends for robust human keypoint tracking
Smoothed temporal keypoint trajectories and engineered motion features from joint geometry and movement cues
Built sequence-modeling and classification pipelines for recognizing actions from pose dynamics
Prepared inference components for real-time or near-real-time application workflows
results: Improved stability of pose-based analysis under challenging video conditions
Built a reusable foundation for action recognition, sports analytics, exercise analysis, ergonomics, and human-computer interaction
Connected pose estimation and temporal classification into a product-oriented inference workflow

title: 3D Point Cloud Registration & Object Alignment
one_liner: Align 3D scans and meshes using point-cloud registration, coarse-to-fine geometry matching, and robust preprocessing.
problem: 3D applications often require accurate alignment between scans or meshes, but noisy geometry, partial overlap, and imperfect initial orientation can make registration unreliable.
approach: Prepared mesh and point-cloud inputs from common 3D data formats
Applied coarse-to-fine registration using RANSAC, FGR, and ICP-style techniques
Used geometric feature processing and learned 3D representations where appropriate
Focused on alignment stability across imperfect scans and varied initialization conditions
results: Created a reusable 3D registration workflow for scan-to-scan and object-alignment tasks
Improved preprocessing reliability for downstream measurement, visualization, reconstruction, and analysis
Established a general workflow applicable to medical, industrial, robotics, and 3D inspection use cases

title: Real-Time Object Detection with YOLO
one_liner: Train and deploy real-time object detection models with YOLO, optimized inference, APIs, and containerized serving.
problem: Computer-vision applications need object detection that remains accurate while also meeting latency, throughput, and deployment constraints.
approach: Trained and fine-tuned YOLOv8 detection models using data augmentation and iterative evaluation
Optimized inference using ONNX, TensorRT, and CUDA-oriented deployment paths
Built image and video inference workflows with OpenCV and Ultralytics
Served predictions through API-based workflows and containerized packaging
results: Created a production-oriented object-detection pipeline for real-time image and video use cases
Prepared deployment-friendly model artifacts for GPU-accelerated inference
Built a reusable serving pattern for monitoring, inspection, analytics, and automation applications

title: Real-Time Instance Segmentation with YOLO
one_liner: Train and deploy segmentation models for pixel-level visual understanding, inspection, measurement, and automation tasks.
problem: Many computer-vision problems require exact object boundaries rather than simple bounding boxes, especially for measurement, inspection, defect analysis, and scene understanding.
approach: Trained and fine-tuned YOLO segmentation models with data augmentation and dataset-quality improvements
Evaluated model behavior using IoU, precision, recall, and task-relevant visual checks
Built OpenCV-based inference workflows for images and video
Prepared ONNX and TensorRT exports for optimized deployment
results: Created a reusable segmentation pipeline for pixel-level computer-vision applications
Established an optimized path from training and evaluation to real-time inference deployment
Built a foundation applicable to visual inspection, measurement, medical imaging, and industrial automation

title: Generative 3D Pipeline with Diffusion Models
one_liner: Explore text- and image-guided 3D generation using diffusion models, LoRA, ControlNet, neural rendering, and modern 3D representations.
problem: Creating detailed 3D assets manually is time-consuming and requires specialized skills, while generative methods can accelerate ideation, texturing, reconstruction, and prototyping.
approach: Used diffusion-based guidance methods such as Stable Diffusion, ControlNet, and LoRA for controllable visual generation
Explored 3D representations and reconstruction approaches including NeRF-style, splatting-inspired, and mesh-based workflows
Combined PyTorch3D, Open3D, Blender, and web-based 3D technologies for experimentation and visualization
Connected research components into prototype interfaces for end-to-end testing
results: Created a research-oriented pipeline for faster 3D asset ideation and prototyping
Built a reusable experimental foundation for generative 3D, reconstruction, and interactive visualization workflows
Evaluated multiple modern components for bridging 2D generative models with 3D content creation

title: CNN Image Classification with Transfer Learning
one_liner: Build robust image-classification pipelines with CNNs, transfer learning, fine-tuning, data augmentation, and API-based deployment.
problem: Image-classification systems must handle variation in lighting, image quality, class imbalance, backgrounds, and visual ambiguity while still producing reliable predictions on unseen data.
approach: Built end-to-end preprocessing, normalization, contrast-enhancement, and data-augmentation pipelines
Trained CNN classifiers and transfer-learning models using established architectures including AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and ResNet
Fine-tuned pretrained networks and compared model behavior across architectures
Applied class-balancing and threshold-aware evaluation to improve robustness on imbalanced datasets
Connected the trained model with a FastAPI-based application workflow for practical inference
results: Created a reusable deep-learning image-classification pipeline from preprocessing through deployment
Improved model robustness for noisy, low-quality, and visually challenging image samples
Built a transferable workflow suitable for medical imaging, quality inspection, product classification, and other image-recognition tasks
